item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-19: reverse-function
item.description:
# Reverse-a-function drill — 2026-11-19
Target: Windows x86-64 (args in `ecx`, `edx`; return in `eax`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: add ecx, edx mov eax, -1 cmovnc eax, ecx ret ```
What does it return for (10, 20) and for (0xFFFFFFF0, 0x20)?
---
## Answer
```c unsigned mystery(unsigned a, unsigned b) { unsigned sum = a + b; return (sum < a) ? 0xFFFFFFFFu : sum; // saturating unsigned add } ```
Results: 30, and 0xFFFFFFFF (the true sum 0x1_0000_0010 doesn't fit in 32 bits).
## Explanation
- `add` sets the carry flag (CF) when the *unsigned* result wraps past 2^32; that's the overflow signal here, not OF (which is for signed). - `mov eax, -1` loads the "max" fallback. `mov` never changes flags, so CF from the `add` survives to the next instruction. - `cmovnc` ("move if no carry") overwrites eax with the sum only when nothing wrapped; otherwise eax stays 0xFFFFFFFF. Result: the sum clamps at UINT_MAX instead of wrapping, with no branch.
